problem.statement: Owners and operators of commercial rooftop photovoltaic systems need to distinguish expected yield variation, data-quality problems, faults, and longer-term degradation using defensible measurement and models. This is a general engineering need, not an identified Taiwan customer's purchase request.

sources.claim: The U.S. DOE describes PV monitoring, modeled benchmarks, performance-ratio reports, alarms, and independent third-party monitoring as established practices; this does not prove unmet buyer demand.
A 2026 literature review identifies cost, uncertainty, testing and lifecycle-analysis limitations in published low-cost photovoltaic monitoring studies.
A 2025 review identifies practical constraints for cost-effective distributed-PV fault diagnosis, including data availability and gaps in real-world validation.

repository.description: Community-maintained Python library of photovoltaic system simulation and performance-modeling functions, suitable as a technical component but not a complete monitoring or audit service.

fit.documented_capability: pvlib-python supplies open photovoltaic modeling functions that can help establish modeled expected generation when configured with relevant system and weather data.
fit.problem_requirement: An independent performance-assessment service would need validated site and inverter data, uncertainty analysis, weather inputs, detection of data gaps and curtailment, independently checked energy-accounting logic, and an actionable human-reviewed report.
fit.unverified_gap: No paid buyer, site data rights, field-calibrated audit implementation, uncertainty-budget validation, site-specific financial savings, or competitive advantage over Raptor Maps and Solargis is established. pvlib alone does not supply this complete service.

market.buyer_segment: Small commercial rooftop PV owners, O&M contractors, and installers who might commission an independent second opinion (unverified segment)
